summary: Tested the Berlin (Navya) fix for international phone formatting. Unit tests (34/34): _format_phone keeps the country code of numbers written with +/00 (Malta, Lithuania, Oman, +49 0176 -> 49176…, US, UK, UAE). It strips 'p:' and \u202a/\u202c, adds 49 to bare Berlin numbers and 91 to bare India numbers, and leaves +91 as-is in both accounts. _clean_phone('berlin') returns +intl and the India path keeps 10 digits. _send_via_aisensy 'destination' was checked by monkeypatching httpx.AsyncClient.post (no network): the UC key gives the 49 default, other keys give 91. E2E as navya: connected the NON-EU (115 rows) and EU (13 rows) tabs and synced each once with send_to_existing=false (0 WhatsApp queued, 127 skipped + 1 duplicate). All 128 stored phones start with + and match their own country code: +49 (47), +356 (15), +36 (18), +371 (8), +968 (1), +91 (Indian numbers that were already +91), +92, +351, +420, +880, +977, +48, +359 and others. No German or other foreign number was turned into a 91 number. The Campaign Leads UI for Navya shows 128 leads, and searching for Oman/Malta numbers works. Cleanup done: campaign_sheets=0, campaign_leads=0.

minor.issue: Bare short local numbers in the real sheet that have no country code and are not 10-11 digits get no country code added. They are stored and would be sent as-is: 'p:99856137' -> +99856137 (invalid), 'p:27831710' -> +27831710 (would go to South Africa), 'p:512805365' -> +512805365 (Peru), 'p:99572336' -> +99572336. These are probably Malta/Latvia/Lithuania local numbers. Consider marking numbers shorter than 10 digits without +/00 as 'invalid phone' instead of sending them.
A bare 10-digit Indian mobile in a Berlin sheet (e.g. '9876543210') becomes +499876543210. This follows the spec, but it is ambiguous. Meta sheets mostly use +cc, so the impact is low.

In the India account, an international number whose digits total exactly 10 (e.g. Singapore +65 9123 4567 -> '6591234567') gets 91 prepended, because _clean_phone drops the '+' and loses the international marker. This is old behaviour that was kept on purpose, so it is noted only.

issues: The Phone column shows the raw sheet value ('p:+491774627243') instead of the cleaned lead.phone ('+491774627243'). Consider showing lead.phone.
The header subtitle on the Campaign Leads page still reads '0 total leads · University change', which is the count from the Leads page, while the table shows 128 campaign leads.

critical_code_review_comments: _format_phone: the intl regex ^\D*(\+|00) correctly allows 'p:' and bidi marks before the '+'. The trunk-0 strip loop only covers 91/49/44/1. For example '+356 0…' would not be stripped, but that is rare.
_send_via_bsp still calls _format_phone(to_phone) with default 91. This is fine for India only.
server.py is 5081 lines and should be split into modules.

success_rate.backend: 100% (35/35 unit + e2e checks; one test failed first only because my threshold was set too high, and the data was correct)

seed_data_creation: Created 2 campaign sheets (TEST_NON-EU, TEST_EU) for navya and 128 leads. All were deleted through the DELETE API. Final counts: campaign_sheets=0, campaign_leads=0.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The E2E test syncs each tab exactly once (the first sync never sends WhatsApp). Do NOT re-sync an existing sheet: a second sync sends real AiSensy messages to new rows. Set KEEP_TEST_SHEETS=1 to keep the sheets for a UI check, then delete them through the API. A sidebar click on 'Campaign Leads' text works; the [data-testid=campaign-leads-tab] selector was not found or visible in the sidebar.
